subject: Design: mTLS pinning + OCSP cache strategy for private endpoints
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme-finance.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme IT <it@acme-finance.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 17:13:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoints - pinning / OCSP / rotation questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for last week's rundown. As we start mapping our internal routing for the Redwood private endpoint (tenant-specific FQDNs), our InfoSec team raised a few items we'd like to confirm before sign-off:

1) Certificate pinning: we understand Redwood wants to keep the ability to swap trust anchors for outage mitigation. Can we get a recommended pinning strategy for long-lived tenant FQDNs that preserves quick recovery while preventing silent MITM?

2) OCSP stapling/caching: some of our edge validators will be intermittently offline. What level of OCSP caching do you expect from the client side vs. the endpoint? Any guidance on stapling TTLs and how Redwood manages OCSP responder availability?

3) CSR automation + HSM: we prefer CSR generation on our side with private keys in our HSM. Does your private deployment support BYOK-compatible CSR workflows and key import for client (m)TLS?

We attached a short matrix of our current expectations (acme_tls_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a sample CSR we generate for other vendors (example_csr_requests.pem).

Appreciate any specifics — InfoSec wants a short one-page decision doc to pass to procurement.

Thanks,
John
John Doe
Network Security Lead, Acme Finance

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme-finance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 19:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoints - pinning / OCSP / rotation questions

John — thanks for the clear list and the matrix, very helpful. I summarized answers below and added action items. I'll convert to a one-page decision doc and share once we've agreed on the details.

Short answers up front:
- Pinning: recommend short-lived pin sets + handshake-level SNI validation rather than permanent public-key pins. We support a two-tier pin approach: (1) operational pin on the proxy layer (auto-updated by Redwood) and (2) optional tenant-provided key pin for high-risk customers.
- OCSP: Redwood will staple OCSP from our delegated responder; we recommend client caches honor stapled responses and fall back to soft-fail only if stapled response is present but validation metadata indicates expiry (we'll provide exact TTL recommendations).
- CSR/HSM: private deploy supports CSR-only onboarding (we accept PEM CSRs), and we can configure the runtime to use customer-supplied keys kept in a customer KMS/HSM via standard BYOK connectors (KMIP, AWS KMS external key references).

Expanded notes / tradeoffs:
1) Pinning approach (detailed)
- Why avoid permanent public-key pins: revocation or necessary rotation (compromise, CA issues) can cause widespread breakage.
- Two-tier operational model:
  * Proxy-tier pin: Redwood-managed pin (rotates on a scheduled window). This lets us preserve automatic fallback if a CA path becomes unavailable. We publish pin roll schedules in the console (and alerting hooks).
  * Tenant-supplied pin (optional): Acme can upload a tenant key thumbprint to the private control plane. This is enforced at the tenant SNI match; if the thumbprint mismatches, we fail the handshake. This is ideal for very sensitive flows but requires a documented emergency rotation process.
- Emergency rotation: we'll support a short-lived “break-glass” intermediate cert (12-24 hours) signed by Redwood's emergency intermediate to avoid customer downtime during manual key swaps.

2) OCSP stapling + caching
- Redwood will staple OCSP responses at the edge for every TLS handshake when available. Staple TTL recommendation: 4–8 minutes for high-frequency endpoints; up to 1 hour for low-frequency backends. We will maintain a cache with proactive revalidation.
- Client-side guidance: honor stapled responses as authoritative. If no staple present, clients doing strict revocation checking should query the OCSP responder; non-strict clients can soft-fail after a configurable window.
- Offline-responder mitigation: we provide an OCSP responder cluster in customer region; for on-prem private deployments we can run a local responder adaptor that mirrors Redwood's responder and accepts signed status tokens.

3) CSR automation and HSM support
- Onboarding options: (A) Customer supplies CSR (we sign/issue and deliver cert chain), (B) Customer supplies certs (we import), (C) Redwood issues certs using delegated CA with proof-of-possession options.
- KMS/HSM integration: supported via connector patterns. Private deployment will not import private keys into Redwood-managed vaults unless customer explicitly allows key escrow. Default pattern: customer keeps keys in their HSM and we use external KMS references.

Action items I propose:
- Marissa: write the one-page decision doc (target: Monday).
- Karthik & Mina: tech checklist for tenant pin upload API + emergency rotation flow (target: next Wed).
- John/Acme: confirm whether tenant-supplied pins are required (yes/no) and which KMS/HSM vendor you're using.

I'll follow up with a short diagram and the console UX steps.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks, that covers most of it. A couple clarifications from InfoSec:

- For the tenant-supplied pin, we need a documented emergency rotation runbook that includes an automated verification step before the pin is enforced (to avoid accidental lockouts).
- OCSP staple TTL of 5 minutes sounds good for our high-throughput endpoints; can you share expected CPU/memory overhead for maintaining revalidation at that cadence?
- HSMs: we're AWS Nitro KMS + on-prem Thales for vaulted keys. We prefer the CSR-only onboarding model and will not export private keys.

If you can include the quick perf numbers and a short runbook draft in the decision doc, we can circulate to procurement.

Also attaching an updated column in the matrix with our preferred settings (acme_tls_matrix_v2.xlsx — see column G).

— John

Subject: Re: Private endpoints - pinning / OCSP / rotation questions

John — perfect, thanks for the quick turn. We'll include the perf numbers and a draft runbook in the one-pager. Quick notes to set expectations:

- Perf ballpark for 5-minute staple cadence (per region edge cluster): ~3–5% CPU increase on the proxy layer and ~150–300MB extra memory for the in-memory OCSP cache for a mid-size cluster (10–15k TPS to TLS edge). We'll confirm with SRE for your expected traffic numbers.
- Emergency rotation runbook (draft):
  1) Customer raises emergency rotation via console API (or signed ticket).
  2) Redwood issues a time-bound intermediate and notifies both customer and SRE on-call.
  3) Temporary intermediate deployed to edge; tenant pin acceptance window is paused for 30 minutes while monitoring runs.
  4) Customer completes key swap in HSM and uploads new thumbprint; Redwood verifies via challenge-response.
  5) Old intermediate revoked and new thumbprint enforced.

I'll produce the one-page decision doc with these bullets + a small sequence diagram and share a draft link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/priv-deploy-acme-tls-design (will add INFRA-2441 to the doc).

Action items (updated):

- Mina: confirm OCSP responder adapter architecture for on-prem and estimate resource numbers (Wed).
- John: confirm HSM vendors (you mentioned AWS Nitro + Thales) and whether tenant pin is required.

I'll loop in SRE after Marissa's draft.

Thanks again,
Rishi
